displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that resurrection merits preference only if a carefully delimited early evidential core is substantially more expected under purposive divine action than under the strongest combined natural account.

novelty.explanation: This narrows the live superiority claim and incorporates the strongest prior-probability objection rather than presuming comprehensive fit.

premises.text: The relevant evidence should be divided by date, source independence, and descriptive specificity before any explanation receives credit for covering it.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the earlier tendency to merge Pauline belief, appearance tradition, and later narrative detail.

premises.text: Early individual and group appearance traditions, bodily-resurrection interpretation, costly proclamation, and any defensible burial evidence should be assessed cumulatively while dependencies are explicitly discounted.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's cumulative case while adding an explicit safeguard against double-counting dependent evidence.

premises.text: A purposive resurrection hypothesis requires independent antecedent support for a capable divine agent and a reason that this particular act would advance the attributed purpose.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the unique-reference-class response by retaining agent-specific and intention-specific prior requirements.

premises.text: Natural alternatives should be compared as a coherent combined model, with each mechanism assigned only the evidence it can explain without unsupported historical reconstruction.

novelty.explanation: This replaces an abbreviated rival comparison with a disciplined test of the strongest interacting natural mechanisms.

premises.text: If the combined natural model requires several weakly evidenced transitions while resurrection predicts the independently supported core under a defended divine purpose, resurrection gains comparative support.

novelty.explanation: This makes the comparative inference conditional on evidenced transitions and a defended purpose rather than on unity alone.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, the historical case may favor resurrection only to the extent that source criticism preserves an independent cumulative core and a defended divine-purpose model predicts that core better than combined natural mechanisms.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately limits the affirmative claim to what the repaired evidential and methodological premises can support.

newArguments.title: Dependency-adjusted convergence
newArguments.text: Several reports should not be counted as independent merely because they appear in different documents. The affirmative can instead construct a dependency graph distinguishing early formula, Pauline interpretation, later narrative elaboration, and genuinely separate attestation. If distinct evidential streams still converge on appearances, bodily interpretation, and physical absence after shared ancestry is discounted, that residual convergence becomes more probative than an undifferentiated list of sources. This method also makes the argument vulnerable to transparent source-critical correction.

novelty.explanation: The transcript did not present a formal dependency-adjusted convergence method for evaluating overlap among evidential streams.

newArguments.title: Comparative transition accounting
newArguments.text: Every explanation can be evaluated by the number and evidential quality of transitions it needs: experience to identification, identification to bodily interpretation, interpretation to group proclamation, and proclamation to developed narrative. Resurrection should receive no automatic advantage, but a natural model should not receive one merely by distributing these transitions across familiar mechanisms. The better account is the one whose required transitions have stronger independent analogues and fewer case-specific assumptions after source uncertainty is included.

novelty.explanation: This adds a symmetric transition-accounting test absent from the participants' stated explanatory comparisons.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that historians should withhold preference for resurrection when source uncertainty and antecedent probability leave a family of ordinary, mutually compatible processes collectively adequate to explain the surviving testimony.

novelty.explanation: This avoids requiring one overprecise natural reconstruction and frames the conclusion as proportionate historical withholding.

premises.text: The earliest sources establish resurrection belief and appearance tradition more securely than they establish detailed, independently witnessed physical encounters or verified bodily absence.

novelty.explanation: This develops the distinction between secure belief content and less secure physical-event detail.

premises.text: Later narrative specificity should receive claim-level scrutiny because literary development can preserve historical memory, reshape it, or combine both processes within the same document.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the categorical Gospel verdict by adopting a mixed and claim-specific source model.

premises.text: Religious visions, suggestion, social reinforcement, interpretive tradition, and ordinary disappearance are independently familiar processes that can interact without every proposed detail occurring exactly as reconstructed.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the natural mechanisms while removing unnecessary confidence in one detailed historical sequence.

premises.text: Probable sincerity supports genuine conviction but remains evidentially neutral between a veridical encounter and an honestly mistaken religious interpretation unless further discriminating evidence is established.

novelty.explanation: This extends the transcript's strongest concession-and-limitation concerning costly proclamation.

premises.text: A divine resurrection model must specify a credible agent, intention, and disclosure policy before the observed restriction of appearances can count as expected rather than retrospectively accommodated.

novelty.explanation: This retains the distributional challenge without claiming certainty about what every compassionate deity would do.

conclusion.text: Therefore, unless independently supported physical evidence and a defensible divine-purpose model discriminate resurrection from the ordinary-process family, the surviving testimony warrants sincere early belief more securely than a historical resurrection conclusion.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion combines the evidential threshold, sincerity distinction, and agent-intention prior into a restrained negative position.

newArguments.title: Robustness across natural models
newArguments.text: The negative need not prove one detailed chain from Peter's experience to every later narrative. It can test whether the main evidential outputs recur across several plausible model combinations: private visions plus social reinforcement, bereavement experiences plus scriptural interpretation, or disappearance plus later narrative development. If resurrection becomes preferable only after every natural model receives an unnecessarily rigid specification, the comparison is unstable. Robust historical preference should survive reasonable variation within the competing model family.

novelty.explanation: The transcript offered particular mechanisms but not a robustness analysis across a structured family of natural models.

newArguments.title: Information-loss asymmetry
newArguments.text: Sparse early reports and richer later narratives create an information-loss problem: many different originating events can produce the same compressed creed, while later detail may reflect memory, interpretation, or composition. Because reconstruction is many-to-one in the early stage and one-to-many in later elaboration, confidence should track features preserved across both transitions. This does not prove a natural origin, but it limits how strongly specific physical details can discriminate resurrection unless those details have independent early support.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an information-loss framework for explaining why sparse early and detailed later sources constrain historical discrimination.
